# Customer Orders Bootstrap Clause

Customer Orders Bootstrap Clause prepares keyed requirements for a customer Order that will be bootstrapped through ordinary Core and then provided to the host document. It is the hosted bootstrap profile; the historical embedded Customer Orders Clause is a separate type. This clause prepares and checks documents. Its preparation result does not by itself mean that an Order has been bootstrapped, accepted by its required parties, confirmed for fulfilment, or paid.

The definition's parameter defaults are prepareFor: bootstrap, obtain: provide, suppliedBy: partner and suppliedParties: [customer]. Its allowedFields default is [orderDescription, amountMinor, customerAccountId, quote, quoteBlueId, orderSnapshot, orderRequest]. Effective parameters come from the configured clause in the document. A new customer-order request requires bootstrap mode and exactly the customer supplied-party slot. Bootstrap mode also requires obtain: provide and an empty inheritChannels list; changing configuration cannot turn this action into an embedded create operation.

The clause is keyed, writes selected Orders at the configured collection binding and keeps preparation entries separately under /process_<clause key>/entries, indexed by the Blue identity of the request key. There is no default collection path. Binding defaults are quotes: /quotes, fulfilment: /clauses/fulfilment/parameters, parties: {seller: seller, partner: partner}, and sources: {}. These are defaults, not assertions about any particular document. The template binding is optional and snapshotted by the connection plan: an explicit parameters.template takes precedence over that captured template. The effective template must exist and satisfy the constructor's checks.

prepare and startOrder both use the same checked customer-order input. They accept only key, requestId, customer, quoteKey, description and groups; key, requestId, customer and quoteKey are required. Key, requestId and quoteKey use the native identifier validator: nonempty text of at most 64 characters, without slash or tilde, without a leading dollar sign, and excluding reserved identifier names. customer must be nonempty text of at most 256 characters and must differ from the current seller and partner myosAccountId values. description defaults to Order and must contain 1 to 300 characters. The customer value is used as the Order's customerAccountId; this prose neither resolves an account nor authorizes a caller.

The selected quote must exist at the configured quotes binding. The clause copies that exact quote, its Blue identity and totalMinor into the prepared Order; callers cannot submit an arbitrary amount through prepare or startOrder. If the configured fulfilment location exists, the request also freezes its terms together with the host description, quote and group selections in orderSnapshot. Native terms and group validation applies, including future proposed starts when the terms require dates. Supplying groups without such a fulfilment configuration is rejected. The constructor copies the configured fulfilment template clauses, clears reservation state, adds the confirmation initialization channel and records the prepared seller/customer information in the snapshot. Supplier confirmation of dates remains a separate process.

Construction requires an uninitialized Order template with the expected Activation Clause and without pre-existing timelineAccess or activation accessPaths. Party mappings retain the mapped native parties while preparing fresh child transports; the customer is the supplied role. Configured fulfilment template clauses can overlay the Order template's clauses, including activation. Provision checks required approvers against the resulting frozen prepared activation policy. It applies only allowed fields and rejects reserved structural fields. If the prepared amountMinor is zero, it removes the child payment clause. It adds creationIntent and a stable instanceKey derived from the host's initialized document identity, clause key and request key. Configured sourcePaths must name initialized sources, and configured identityChildren must be uninitialized templates. Configured named sources use the native declaration, mapping, activity and access checks. None of this code performs the later Core bootstrap or substitutes a manual channel binder.

An existing preparation with the same key and exactly the same original customer-order request returns duplicate; changed input for that key is rejected. A new request also rejects an occupied destination or missing party mapping. With the required provide mode, acceptance stores the prepared requirements, original request, customer identity, exact commercial and fulfilment terms, provider slots and requirementRef; its initial status is awaiting_provider. It emits Document Prepared as a preparation-status notification. It separately emits Document Provision Requested to the configured suppliedBy party (partner by default), requesting the next work. Neither event confirms that the provider supplied an Order or that execution completed.

provide is correlated to the recorded key, inResponseTo request identifier and requirementRef, and must arrive on the recorded supplier channel. Its declared defaults are key: single and empty inResponseTo, requirementRef and document; an actual keyed obligation still needs matching values and an initialized candidate document. Provision rejects an unreviewed source, changed effective clause policy, invalid provider specializations, or missing native bootstrap access evidence. The bootstrap checks retain the mapped actors and representative roster and require initialized access documents for the candidate's full transport roster. The candidate must preserve the frozen customerAccountId, quote, quoteBlueId, amountMinor and orderSnapshot, and both its current and initialized customer identity must match the frozen customer. A previously selected origin cannot be replaced by another origin.

A provided candidate can remain admission_pending, awaiting_activation or linking while the corresponding native conditions remain unsatisfied. If it is ready, provision records its origin, selects its Blue reference at the configured collection location and emits Document Selected. resume runs the shared readiness refresh. A selected entry becomes usable only when the selected document is active and its named sources are ready; losing that readiness can return the entry to selected. Document Attached marks the usable transition. These are document preparation and attachment states, not proof of fulfilment, payment or all future business actions. This specialization returns no domain next actions.

cancel defaults its key to single. Before an Order origin is selected, it records cancellation_requested and emits Preparation Cancellation Requested; an identical repeated cancellation request is duplicate. This is a cancellation request, not confirmation that any external work was cancelled. Once an origin has been selected, this generic cancellation is rejected and the Order's own domain cancellation process is required.

For Terms, this explanation describes the exact clause's rules and configurable defaults. Current clause values, party approvals, access, preparation status, selected Order, source readiness and execution results must come from authorized native document reads. Core and the native packages own identities, permissions, bootstrap, execution and timeline truth. Loading this local explanation adds no execution capability, approval, authority or package identity, and makes no claim about the current state of a particular agreement.
